title: 1977 AHSME Problem 19
statement: Let \(E\) be the point of intersection of the diagonals of convex quadrilateral \(ABCD,\) and let \(P,\) \(Q,\) \(R\) and \(S\) be the centers of the circles circumscribing triangles \(ABE,\) \(BCE,\) \(CDE\) and \(ADE,\) respectively. Then

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
\(PQRS\) is a parallelogram if and only if \(ABCD\) is a
rhombus

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
\(PQRS\) is a parallelogram if and only if \(ABCD\) is a
rectangle

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
\(PQRS\) is a parallelogram if and only if \(ABCD\) is a
parallelogram

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: none of the above are true

solutions.text:
Both \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on the perpendicular bisector of \(BE,\) while both \(R\) and \(S\) lie on the perpendicular bisector of \(DE.\) Since \(B,\) \(E,\) \(D\) are collinear, these bisectors are parallel, so \(PQ\parallel RS.\) Likewise, \(Q,\) \(R\) lie on the perpendicular bisector of \(CE,\) and \(S,\) \(P\) lie on that of \(AE.\) Since \(A,\) \(E,\) \(C\) are collinear, \(QR\parallel SP.\) Therefore \(PQRS\) is always a parallelogram.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Two adjacent circumcenters lie on the perpendicular bisector of the side shared by their triangles
Use the fact that \(A,\) \(E,\) \(C\) are collinear and \(B,\) \(E,\) \(D\) are collinear
